newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Firmer amid fall in stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Firmer amid fall in stocks.

text.p: The top end of the barrel firmed with crude amid a fall in Singapore weekly stocks, industry sources said on Thursday.
Light distillates stocks, comprising gasoline, reformate and naphtha, were at 7.315 million barrels on May 21, down 317,000 barrels from the previous week, Singapore's Trade Development Board said.
Naphtha June swaps were quoted at $22.30/$22.60 a barrel, up sharply from Tuesday's $21.90/$22.10, and at a 10 cents contango to July.

Regional demand emerged in the form of Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) tender to buy 28,000-tonnes of naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) naphtha for delivery July 20-31 to Kaohsiung which closes May 28 and is valid for two days, a company official said.
CPC's last tender, for May 11-31 delivery, was awarded at just below $230 per tonne, c-and-f.
Talk on fob Singapore gasoline was lacklustre but prices edged up slightly with crude.
Current fundamentals were still bearish, as evidenced by the low awards in CPC's reformate tender.
CPC bought a second cargo of 95-octane reformate from its tender which closed May 19.
On Tuesday, traders said CPC acquired 250,000 barrels at $24.92 per barrel, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Taiwan for delivery July 1-15.
But CPC sources said on Thursday the company bought a second cargo at $25.20, c-and-f June 21-30.
The purchases were from separate sellers and are for delivery to Keelung or Taichung.
The tender closed May 19 and was valid for two days.
"They were very cheap numbers," a trader said. "That's why they have bought more."
Traders had expected the latest awards to be higher than CPC's last reformate tender because of rising crude values.
Last time, CPC awarded two June 11-30 cargoes at around $25.30 per barrel.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
